title: Crestline Accelerator — API ramp & privacy evaluation
summary: Discovery call for Crestline Accelerator exploring Redwood's PLG/self-serve API onramp and options for moving to Dedicated or Private deployments later. Customer wants quick time-to-first-token for a prototype, clarity on data residency and KMS, and rough cost/latency expectations. Next steps agreed: send security pack, pricing SKUs, and schedule a technical deep dive for benchmarking.
action_items: Maya Lin: Send pricing deck and dedicated capacity SKU sheet - due 2026-06-21
Carlos Ortega: Share benchmark runbook and sample prompt set for latency/cost tests - due 2026-06-22
Nina Patel: Provide sample traffic profile (QPS / typical prompt lengths) and compliance contacts - due 2026-06-24
next_steps: Maya to email SOC2 + security docs and whitepaper link
Schedule 60-min technical deep dive with infra team (Carlos + Ravi + Crestline engs)
Provision PLG free credits and onboard Nina & Devon to org for TTFT sprint
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18 08:00 PDT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (CTO, Crestline Accelerator), Devon Park (ML Eng), Alisha Brooks (Head of Platform)

--- Optional auto-summary (auto):
Quick: Crestline wants to get to a prototype first week, worried about PII and KMS, also wants guidance on when to flip from hosted -> dedicated or private.

00:00 - 00:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for joining uh really excited to chat through how we can get you to first call fast and also map out the security path. Quick intros?
00:31 - 01:10 Speaker 2 (Nina): Hi I'm Nina, CTO at Crestline, we run accelerator programs for seed startups and also operate a shared infra for portfolio companies. We're looking to build a prototype for our startup ops dashboard so want TTFT and controls for data residency.
01:11 - 01:45 Speaker 3 (Devon): Hey devon here, I'm the ML eng, mostly going to run prompts against user metadata, some PII in the vectors, so encryption and KMS matter.
01:46 - 02:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, thanks. I'm Maya and I'll be the AE, with Carlos and Ravi joining to cover architecture and benchmarks. At a high level our PLG flow is: self-serve API, free credits to try, then you can bump to Reserved/Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) as needed.
02:21 - 03:05 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Hi all, quick note on the runtime: our serving engine does batching, KV cache, quantized variants. For small prototypes hosted is usually easiest and fastest TTFT, dedicated helps when you want predictable throughput and private is for strict compliance.
03:06 - 03:50 Speaker 2 (Nina): Okay can you give rough numbers—latency and cost—for hosted vs dedicated for say a 2k token request with an open model?
03:51 - 04:40 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Sure rough ballpark: hosted with optimized open model 2k tokens, tail latency maybe 300-700ms per token sequence (depends on concurrency). For dedicated you get lower tail and consistent p95s since you control pool. Cost... it's a bit variable but we can share SKU sheet and sample calc.
04:41 - 05:15 Speaker 3 (Devon): Sorry when you say "KV cache" can you explain—the type of cache we should expect? Like are we storing prefix K-V in customer tenant?
05:16 - 06:05 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Good question. KV cache is handled in the runtime; for hosted it's cached at the tenant level in our runtime with TTLs; for private or dedicated we can expose options to keep KV local to your VPC. Sometimes the auto-transcript picks up K-V as 'K-V cash' so ignore that note :)
06:06 - 06:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): On the credits side we usually provision a PLG bucket for builders—enough to run a couple hundred calls and test throughput. That gets you to first token pretty quickly. We also provide quickstart guides and a sample repo.
06:51 - 07:30 Speaker 2 (Nina): What's the onboarding look like? Can our engineers self-serve or do you need a hand from Redwood?
07:31 - 08:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): Most teams self-serve. We have SDKs, curl examples, and a step-by-step TTFT checklist. For customers that want it we also do a hand-holding onboarding session.
08:11 - 09:00 Speaker 5 (Alisha): From platform side I'm thinking about network egress and VPC peering later—if we start hosted and then move to VPC, how painless is that?
09:01 - 09:50 Speaker 4 (Carlos): We try to keep the API surface consistent: same endpoints, same SDKs. Moving from hosted to VPC involves setting up the private control plane and network configs, we'll support a canary rollout. There are some infra tasks but we handle the orchestration and rollout policies.
09:51 - 10:40 Speaker 3 (Devon): For privacy, is data at rest encrypted by default? And can we bring our own KMS?
10:41 - 11:30 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Yes data at rest is encrypted; you can bring your own KMS in Private deployments. For Hosted we use our managed keys but we have HSM integrations for enterprise. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs.
11:31 - 12:15 Speaker 2 (Nina): What's the SLA on hosted? We're okay with best-effort for prototype but want to understand uptime for production later.
12:16 - 13:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hosted has standard uptime SLAs for paid tiers, dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll include the SLA table in the pricing deck.
13:01 - 14:00 Speaker 5 (Alisha): Any limitations on embeddings / vector store usage? We plan to store aggregated user embeddings and some of them include hashed PII. How is retention managed?
14:01 - 15:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Retention policies are configurable. For hosted we offer configurable retention windows and purge endpoints; for private deployments you retain full control. Also note that transcription might sometimes flip "KV cache" to other phrasing—worth double-checking the notes.
15:01 - 16:00 Speaker 3 (Devon): Competitors question—how do you compare on cost vs OpenAI for inference?
16:01 - 17:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): For open models we often beat the managed closed-provider cost on a per-token basis especially once you start batching and caching. Anthropic and others vary. We'll share a cost projection template that models batching ratios and token lengths.
17:11 - 19:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): If you expect bursty traffic it's worth looking at dedicated with burst capacity. Also quantized model variants can reduce GPU cost with minor quality tradeoffs, we can show examples.
19:01 - 20:00 Speaker 2 (Nina): How quickly can we get a test organization with credits? If we get creds today can we call the API by tomorrow?
20:01 - 21:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes typically we can provision PLG credits and accounts same-day; TTFT often within a few hours if you follow the quickstart.
21:01 - 22:00 Speaker 5 (Alisha): Any compliance caveats for EU data residency? We're hosting some workloads in Frankfurt region.
22:01 - 23:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): We have region-based deployments and can route requests to specific regions. For strict residency we recommend private deploy in the region or dedicated capacity pinned to that region; we'll include the region options doc.
23:01 - 24:30 Speaker 3 (Devon): For the benchmark deep dive, what telemetry do you need from us? Sample QPS, avg token lengths, concurrency?
24:31 - 25:20 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Exactly—QPS, concurrency, typical prompt distribution, desired p95 latency. Also any policy triggers for fallbacks. We'll provide a benchmark runbook that maps to our kernel selection and batching profiles.
25:21 - 26:30 Speaker 2 (Nina): On security reviews—who signs the DPA? Is there standard language for startups?
26:31 - 27:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have a standard DPA for customers; for enterprise we can negotiate additional clauses. For now we'll send the standard DPA and SOC2 report.
27:41 - 29:00 Speaker 5 (Alisha): Curious—how is observability surfaced? Do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-model dashboards?
29:01 - 30:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Yes Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency, traces, error rates. You can set alerts on quality regressions too.
30:01 - 31:20 Speaker 2 (Nina): Any gotchas for multi-tenant setups since we run many startups in one org?
31:21 - 33:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Multi-tenant is common; we recommend RBAC, per-team token buckets, and isolated projects. If eventual data isolation is required, dedicated pools per-tenant or private deployments are options.
33:01 - 35:00 Speaker 3 (Devon): Alright for the TTFT sprint, could you outline the minimal checklist to be runnable?
35:01 - 36:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): Minimal: create org/account, provision API keys, run curl sample, hit endpoints with sample prompt, confirm embeddings and responses, run a couple of tokenized requests to measure latency. We have a TTFT checklist in docs and a sample repo.
36:11 - 37:20 Speaker 2 (Nina): Sounds good. Can you also include a cost estimate for 10k calls per day vs 100k?
37:21 - 38:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes we'll include a cost-vs-usage sheet with assumptions about batching and average token length.
38:11 - 40:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): For the technical deep dive let's book an hour next Wed, we'll ask you to share sample prompts and a small dataset so we can run the runbook.
40:01 - 41:00 Speaker 2 (Nina): We'll coordinate internally and get the sample traffic and compliance contact.
41:01 - 42:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap: Maya will send security pack (SOC2, DPA, KMS notes), pricing and SKU sheet, Carlos to send benchmark runbook and sample prompt set, provisioning of PLG credits for Nina and Devon. Next meeting: technical deep dive Wednesday (proposed) - Maya will follow up with calendar invite. Thanks everyone.

Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/ttft-quickstart (sample), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (SOC2 doc), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/runbook (benchmark runbook)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hears: 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K-V cash', 'on-prem' might appear as 'on premise'. Names occasionally garbled.
